info.description:
Records US stock trades and tracks portfolio cost and P&L. It does not place real orders.
Phase 1 covers sign-up with email verification (OTP), login and logout with a server-side session cookie, Google sign-in and linking, password reset (OTP), many portfolios per user, recording, editing and deleting buys and sells, and holdings and valuation with delayed prices: sample prices in demo mode (PRICE_PROVIDER=demo) and delayed SIP prices from Alpaca when PRICE_PROVIDER=alpaca. Dividends, splits, mergers and symbol changes are not handled, and results are not tax reports.
info.title: Stock Portfolio Tracker API

get.description: Tells a client whether Google sign-in is configured. When google_enabled is false, the Google endpoints answer 503 feature_disabled.

500.description: internal, such as a recovered panic

get.description: Returns the token to send in the X-CSRF-Token header of every POST. Signed in, the token is bound to the session; signed out, it is bound to a random nonce that this call keeps in the HttpOnly cookie csrf_nonce (__Host-csrf_nonce over HTTPS). Tokens last one hour. Ask for a new token after login and after logout, because the binding changes. Browsers (and Swagger UI) send the cookie by themselves; curl needs a cookie jar (-b/-c).

Set-Cookie.description: csrf_nonce=…; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax — only when signed out

503.description: dependency_unavailable: the session store could not be reached

post.description: Checks the 6-digit code sent by register or by "send a new code". A wrong, expired, already used or exhausted code (5 wrong tries) gives the same 400 invalid_verification. Success verifies the email but does not sign in: call POST /api/v1/auth/login next. Needs X-CSRF-Token and the csrf_nonce cookie.

parameters.description: challenge_id from the 202 response and the 6 ASCII digits from the email
parameters.name: body

post.description: Sends a new 6-digit code to an account that registered with a password and is not verified yet, and invalidates its previous code. The answer is the same for every email, so it does not reveal whether an account exists; register and this endpoint share one quota per email (one code a minute, five an hour). Needs X-CSRF-Token and the csrf_nonce cookie.

parameters.description: The email to send a code to
parameters.name: body

get.description: Google sends the browser here after GET authorization_url. It is not called directly: it needs the state from that URL and the oidc_binding cookie of the browser that started the flow, and it takes no X-CSRF-Token (the state, the binding and the ID token's nonce protect it). It always clears oidc_binding and answers 303 to /docs/?google=success (signed in: the session cookie is set), linked (Google added to the signed-in account), link_required (the email belongs to an account: sign in to it and use POST /api/v1/auth/google/link) or failed (cancelled, expired, replayed, another browser, or refused). Infrastructure failures answer JSON instead.

parameters.description: Set by Google when the user cancelled
parameters.name: error

Set-Cookie.description: oidc_binding=; Expires=Tue, 10 Nov 2009 23:00:00 GMT — and session=… on success

503.description: feature_disabled (Google is not configured) or dependency_unavailable

post.description: Like POST /api/v1/auth/google/start, but the flow belongs to the signed-in user: after Google, the callback adds the Google account to this account (/docs/?google=linked) without opening a new session. The callback must come with the same session. Needs the session cookie and an X-CSRF-Token bound to it.
post.summary: Link Google to the signed-in account

parameters.description: Token from GET /api/v1/auth/csrf, fetched while signed in
parameters.name: X-CSRF-Token

post.description: Returns the Google URL to open in the same browser, and sets the HttpOnly cookie oidc_binding (__Host-oidc_binding over HTTPS) that must come back with the callback; the flow lasts 10 minutes. Google sends the browser to GET /api/v1/auth/google/callback, which ends at /docs/?google=success|link_required|failed. A Google account whose email already belongs to an account is not linked automatically: sign in to that account and use POST /api/v1/auth/google/link. Needs X-CSRF-Token and the csrf_nonce cookie. Swagger UI and curl cannot complete the Google page; open authorization_url in the browser.

503.description: feature_disabled (Google is not configured) or dependency_unavailable (Google cannot be reached)

post.description: Opens a session and sets it in the HttpOnly cookie session (__Host-session over HTTPS; SameSite=Lax, Path=/); the body only describes it. An unknown email, a wrong password and an account that signs in only with Google all give the same 401. The right password of an account whose email is not verified gives 403 email_not_verified. The pre-login csrf_nonce cookie is cleared: call GET /api/v1/auth/csrf again for a token bound to the new session. Needs X-CSRF-Token.
post.summary: Sign in with an email and a password

post.description: Revokes the current session on the server and clears the session cookie. Without an active session (none, expired or already revoked) it only clears the cookie and still answers 204. Needs X-CSRF-Token: signed in, a token bound to the session; otherwise one bound to the csrf_nonce cookie.

Set-Cookie.description: session=; Path=/; Expires=Tue, 10 Nov 2009 23:00:00 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax

get.description: Needs the session cookie from POST /api/v1/auth/login.

503.description: dependency_unavailable: the session store could not be reached

post.description: Replaces the password. Send either reset_token from POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/verify (two steps, recommended: a wrong code is reported before the user picks a password) or challenge_id with otp (one step, still supported); sending both, or neither, is 400 invalid_input. A wrong, expired, used, other-browser or superseded reset_token, and a wrong, expired, already used, exhausted or unknown code, all give the same 400 invalid_reset; a code may be tried wrong 5 times. The new password follows the same rules as register; the rule that it must not contain the part of the email before "@" is checked only after the token or code is accepted, so a refusal never reveals anything about the account, and failing that rule spends neither, so another password can be tried. Each IP address can try 20 times in 15 minutes, shared with verify. Success verifies the email, signs the account out on every device, sends a notice email and does not sign in: call POST /api/v1/auth/login next. Needs X-CSRF-Token and the csrf_nonce cookie.
post.summary: Set a new password with the reset token or the reset code

parameters.description: new_password with either reset_token, or challenge_id and the 6 ASCII digits from the email
parameters.name: body

400.description: invalid_reset, invalid_input (password rules, details lists the reasons; or both or neither of reset_token and challenge_id/otp) or malformed_json

post.description: Sends a 6-digit code, valid for 10 minutes, to an account that has a password, and invalidates the code sent before. The answer is the same for every email, so it does not reveal whether an account exists; an account that signed up only with Google has no password and gets no code. Each email can ask once a minute and five times an hour, and each IP address 20 times an hour. Needs X-CSRF-Token and the csrf_nonce cookie.
post.summary: Ask for a password reset code

parameters.description: The email to send a code to
parameters.name: body

post.description: First step of the two-step reset. Checks the 6-digit code sent by "ask for a password reset code" without changing the password, so a wrong code shows up before the user picks a new password. A code works once and may be tried wrong 5 times, counted together with the one-step confirm; a wrong, expired, already used, exhausted or unknown code all give the same 400 invalid_reset. Each IP address can try 20 times in 15 minutes, shared with confirm. A right code is spent and turned into reset_token: send it with the new password to POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/confirm within expires_in seconds (10 minutes). The token works once, only from the same browser (it is tied to the csrf_nonce cookie, or to the session when signed in), and stops working when a new code is requested. Nothing about the account changes yet. Needs X-CSRF-Token and the csrf_nonce cookie.
post.summary: Check the reset code and get a reset token

parameters.description: challenge_id from the 202 response and the 6 ASCII digits from the email
parameters.name: body

post.description: Creates an unverified account and emails a 6-digit verification code. The answer is the same whether or not the email already has an account: the owner of an existing account gets an email notice instead and nothing changes. The response takes at least about half a second on purpose. Needs the pre-login CSRF flow: call GET /api/v1/auth/csrf first, send its token in X-CSRF-Token, and send the csrf_nonce cookie (a browser does this itself). Then confirm the code with POST /api/v1/auth/email-verification/confirm.
post.summary: Register with an email and a password

parameters.description: Email, and a password of 6-32 printable ASCII characters without spaces, with a lower-case letter, an upper-case letter and a special character
parameters.name: body

400.description: invalid_input (details lists every broken password rule) or malformed_json

get.description: Newest first. Pass the next_cursor of a page as cursor to get the following page; next_cursor is null on the last page. A cursor is opaque and only valid for the user it was issued to. Other users' portfolios never appear.
get.summary: List the portfolios of the signed-in user

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

post.description: Adds a portfolio for the signed-in user. A user can have many portfolios (for example long term, short term and speculative); every portfolio uses USD. The name is trimmed, must be 1-100 characters and must not repeat another portfolio name of the same user, ignoring letter case (409 portfolio_name_conflict); another user may use the same name. The ETag header carries the version to send in If-Match when you change or delete the portfolio. Needs the session cookie and X-CSRF-Token.

ETag.description: The portfolio version number wrapped in double quotes

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

get.description: A portfolio that belongs to someone else gets exactly the same 404 as one that does not exist. The ETag header carries the version to send in If-Match.

ETag.description: The portfolio version number wrapped in double quotes

400.description: invalid_input: portfolio_id is not a UUID

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

put.description: Replaces the name and description: send both, a body without description is refused with 400 and nothing is written (send an empty string to clear it). Send the ETag of your last read in If-Match, for example "3" with the quotes: without it the call is refused with 428 precondition_required; if the portfolio changed since (version_conflict) the call is refused with 412 and nothing is written. Only the exact form "<version>" is accepted: the wildcard *, weak validators (W/"3") and lists give 400. A name that another portfolio of yours already uses, ignoring letter case, gives 409 portfolio_name_conflict; renaming a portfolio to the same name in a different case is allowed. A portfolio of another user gives the same 404 as one that does not exist. Needs the session cookie and X-CSRF-Token.
put.summary: Rename a portfolio or change its description

parameters.description: ETag of the last read: the version number wrapped in double quotes
parameters.name: If-Match

parameters.description: New name and description; description is required, send an empty string to clear it
parameters.name: body

ETag.description: The new version number wrapped in double quotes

400.description: invalid_input (body, portfolio_id or If-Match) or malformed_json

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

delete.description: Deletes a portfolio that has no transactions; a portfolio with transactions is kept and the call gives 409 portfolio_not_empty (history is never deleted silently). Needs If-Match with the ETag of your last read, like PUT. A portfolio of another user gives the same 404 as one that does not exist. Needs the session cookie and X-CSRF-Token.

parameters.description: ETag of the last read: the version number wrapped in double quotes
parameters.name: If-Match

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

get.description: One entry per stock ever traded in the portfolio, sorted by symbol, calculated from its transactions with a moving weighted-average cost. A stock that was sold out stays with quantity "0" because of its realized profit and loss. No prices are used, so this works even when the price provider does not. Numbers are exact decimal strings; round them for display only. A portfolio that belongs to someone else gets exactly the same 404 as one that does not exist. Needs the session cookie.

400.description: invalid_input: portfolio_id is not a UUID

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

get.description: Newest first by executed_at, trades executed at the same time by sequence. Pass the next_cursor of a page as cursor to get the following page; next_cursor is null on the last page. A cursor is opaque and only valid for the portfolio and the filters it was issued for: with other filters it gives 400. symbol, side, from and to narrow the list; an empty value does not filter. from and to include the instant itself. Write a timezone offset such as +02:00 as %2B02:00 in the query. A portfolio of another user gives the same 404 as one that does not exist.
get.summary: List the trades of a portfolio

parameters.description: Only this symbol, for example AAPL
parameters.name: symbol

parameters.description: Only trades executed at or after this RFC 3339 time
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Only trades executed at or before this RFC 3339 time
parameters.name: to

400.description: invalid_input: bad portfolio_id, limit, cursor, symbol, side, from or to

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

post.description: Records a buy or sell the user made elsewhere; this API never places an order. Every field is required. quantity, price and fee are decimal strings (a JSON number is refused with 400 malformed_json): quantity and price must be greater than zero, fee may be "0", and each has at most 10 decimals and 18 digits before the point. executed_at is an RFC 3339 timestamp with a timezone, not in the future and with at most microsecond precision. The symbol is upper-cased; a symbol the API has not seen yet is checked with the instrument provider (422 unknown_symbol when it does not exist, 503 dependency_unavailable when the provider cannot answer, so retry), at most 30 new symbols per user per hour (429 rate_limited). The whole history of the portfolio is replayed in time order: a sale that would leave fewer than zero shares at any point gives 422 insufficient_shares and nothing is written. Idempotency-Key (1-128 visible ASCII characters) is required: the same key with the same trade returns the first result again with 201 and records nothing more; the same key with another trade gives 409 idempotency_conflict. A key keeps its result for 24 hours from the first request. The ETag header carries the version to send in If-Match when the trade is changed or deleted. A portfolio of another user gives the same 404 as one that does not exist. Needs the session cookie and X-CSRF-Token.
post.summary: Record a trade in a portfolio

parameters.description: Unique key of this request, 1-128 visible ASCII characters, for example a UUID
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: The trade; every field is required and numbers are decimal strings
parameters.name: body

ETag.description: The transaction version number wrapped in double quotes

400.description: invalid_input (body, portfolio_id or Idempotency-Key) or malformed_json

409.description: idempotency_conflict: the key was used for another trade

429.description: rate_limited: too many new symbols this hour

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

get.description: A trade in a portfolio of another user, or in another portfolio of yours, gets exactly the same 404 as one that does not exist. The ETag header carries the version to send in If-Match.

ETag.description: The transaction version number wrapped in double quotes

400.description: invalid_input: portfolio_id or transaction_id is not a UUID

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

put.description: Replaces the whole trade: send all six fields (symbol, side, quantity, price, fee, executed_at) with the same rules as when recording it; a body that leaves a field out is refused with 400 and nothing is written. Send the ETag of your last read in If-Match: without it the call is refused with 428 precondition_required; if the trade changed since (version_conflict) the call is refused with 412 and nothing is written. Only the exact form of one version number wrapped in double quotes is accepted: the wildcard, weak validators and lists give 400. The trade stays in its portfolio and keeps its id, sequence and created_at; the version goes up by one. A symbol the API has not seen yet is checked with the instrument provider (422 unknown_symbol, 503 dependency_unavailable, 429 rate_limited) like when recording a trade. The whole history of the portfolio is replayed in time order: a change that would leave fewer than zero shares at any point gives 422 invalid_history and nothing is written. A trade that is not in this portfolio, or in a portfolio of another user, gets the same 404 as one that does not exist. Needs the session cookie and X-CSRF-Token.

parameters.description: ETag of the last read: the version number wrapped in double quotes
parameters.name: If-Match

parameters.description: The whole trade; every field is required and numbers are decimal strings
parameters.name: body

ETag.description: The new version number wrapped in double quotes

400.description: invalid_input (body, portfolio_id, transaction_id or If-Match) or malformed_json

429.description: rate_limited: too many new symbols this hour

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

delete.description: Removes the trade and replays the history of the portfolio: a deletion that would leave fewer than zero shares at any point (for example removing a buy that a later sale needs) gives 422 invalid_history and nothing is written. Needs If-Match with the ETag of your last read, like PUT. A trade that is not in this portfolio, or in a portfolio of another user, gets the same 404 as one that does not exist, and so does a trade that was already deleted. Needs the session cookie and X-CSRF-Token.

parameters.description: ETag of the last read: the version number wrapped in double quotes
parameters.name: If-Match

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; only sent with server_busy, not with dependency_unavailable

get.description: Prices every stock still held with a delayed reference price: the close of the last bar before 15 minutes ago. It is not a bid or ask price and not a price one could trade at. A price that is missing is null and never "0": coverage says whether every stock still held has a price (complete), some do (partial) or none does (unavailable, which is also the answer when the price provider cannot be reached). Unless coverage is complete, market_value and unrealized_pnl are null and priced_market_value is only the subtotal of the priced stocks; realized_pnl and the holdings never depend on prices. unrealized_pnl = quantity x price - remaining cost, without any selling fee. With PRICE_PROVIDER=demo the prices are sample data and is_demo is true. calculated_at is when the transactions were read. A portfolio that belongs to someone else gets exactly the same 404 as one that does not exist. Needs the session cookie.

tags.description: Registration, email verification, sessions and CSRF tokens. Every POST needs the X-CSRF-Token header from GET /api/v1/auth/csrf and must come from the API's own origin.
tags.name: Auth

tags.description: Forgot-password flow with a 6-digit code sent by email: ask for a code, then set a new password with it. The answer to the request is the same for every email. Every POST needs the X-CSRF-Token header from GET /api/v1/auth/csrf and must come from the API's own origin.
tags.name: Password Reset

tags.description: What a portfolio holds and what it is worth, with delayed prices. A price that is missing is null, never zero; realized profit and loss never depends on prices. Read-only, needs the session cookie.
tags.name: Holdings/Prices

tags.description: A user can own many portfolios, all in USD. Every call needs the session cookie; another user's portfolio looks exactly like a missing one (404). Reading returns an ETag with the portfolio version; changing or deleting a portfolio needs it back in If-Match.
tags.name: Portfolios

tags.description: Buys and sells a user recorded in one of their portfolios; the API never places orders. Every call needs the session cookie; a portfolio of another user looks exactly like a missing one (404). Quantity, price and fee are decimal strings. Creating a trade needs an Idempotency-Key, so a retry never records it twice; reading returns an ETag with the trade version.
tags.name: Transactions
